GenreCode.description:
Un genre normalisé : le code d'abord, le libellé comme commodité.

Le code est la valeur STABLE — il survit à un changement de libellé
d'affichage, il est indexable, il tient dans une URL. Le libellé change
avec la langue et l'humeur éditoriale. Rendre le libellé seul obligerait
un client à faire de la chaîne de caractères la clé de son filtre.

IdentityResponse.description:
Ce que l'on sait de l'identité d'une œuvre, et comment on le sait.

Aucun identifiant n'est partagé entre les plateformes : chaque lien est une
DÉCISION, avec une méthode, un score et un statut. Les rendre sans leur
provenance laisserait croire à une jointure.

SeriesResponse.description:
Une série du socle catalogue Manga Sanctuary.

Les colonnes internes du rapprochement (`ms_title_norm_x`,
`_other_titles_list`, `matched_title_norm`, `fuzzy_low_score`…) ne sont PAS
exposées : ce sont des états intermédiaires d'un calcul, pas des faits sur
l'œuvre. Ce que le rapprochement a conclu se lit sur `/identity/{work_uid}`.

annee_fr.description: Year of the first volume with a French EAN.
annee_fr.title: Annee Fr

auteurs.description: The writer then the artist, as written, joined by a comma, the same name once; a textual « inconnu » counts as absent; COLLECTIF stays.
auteurs.title: Auteurs

demographie.description: `series_category_clean`, or `series_category` when it holds a value from the same list (the three Korean categories mapped). The catalogue label, as is.
demographie.title: Demographie

disponibilite.description: `edite_en_france` when a volume carries a French EAN (9782, 97910) or the record carries the « français » badge; `seulement_au_japon` for a Manga with volumes and none of that; `inconnue` otherwise. **Published in France does not mean in stock**: the catalogue knows no stock. The value the model API carries on its cards.
disponibilite.title: Disponibilite

genres_enriched.description: Normalised codes from the genre reference, merging both sources and their hierarchy. **Not** a fallback for `genres_source`: the two answer different questions and neither replaces the other.
genres_enriched.title: Genres Enriched

genres_source.description: Raw Manga Sanctuary labels, in French, exactly as the source wrote them — casing included.
genres_source.title: Genres Source

nb_volumes.description: The larger of the « volumes published » field and the distinct volume numbers (a volume without a number counts as number 1), all editions mixed; a number between 1900 and 2100 is a year from the title and does not count. Read it with `nb_volumes_source`.
nb_volumes.title: Nb Volumes

nb_volumes_source.description: `divergent` when both counts exist and differ by more than 20 % of the larger; `champ` when the field is at least the numbers; `repli_volumes_distincts` otherwise. **Any source other than `champ` reads as a minimum**: « at least N ».
nb_volumes_source.title: Nb Volumes Source

needs_review.description: The identity decision behind this series is flagged for human review. Method, score and reason live on `/identity/{work_uid}`.
needs_review.title: Needs Review

statuses.description: Status badges of the source record, **serialised as collected** (Python-formatted strings). The normalised status is `statut`.
statuses.title: Statuses

statut.description: `termine` on the « Complète » badge or Kitsu `finished`; `en_cours` on Kitsu `current` without the badge. The catalogue never writes « en cours »: no badge does not mean ongoing. `null`: unknown.
statut.title: Statut

synopsis_enriched.description: Manga Sanctuary synopsis, or the Kitsu one when MS has none.
synopsis_enriched.title: Synopsis Enriched

tags_source.description: Raw Manga Sanctuary tags. Open vocabulary, not normalised.
tags_source.title: Tags Source

volume_count.description: Number of edition rows of the series **as recorded in December 2025** (a frozen field of the reference: it may lag behind the catalogue, or be missing). For the number of volumes, read `nb_volumes`.
volume_count.title: Volume Count

work_uid.description: Identity hub key. Use it on `/identity/{work_uid}`.
work_uid.title: Work Uid

info.description:
Read-only HTTP API over the manga corpus stored in PostgreSQL (schema `manga`).

**Authorisation.** Data endpoints require an `X-API-Key` header. The
documentation (`/docs`, `/redoc`, `/openapi.json`) and the probes (`/live`,
`/health`) are open by design: *the documentation is open, the data is closed.*
info.title: API Manga

get.description:
Reference totals, identity decisions by method, and genre coverage — **including the known limits**.

Two of them are structural and will not be fixed by any further work: 1 694 series carry no genre in *either* source, and 526 series carry only the generic `lgbt` code because no reliable Kitsu match exists to refine it. Both are reported here rather than left for a reader to discover.
get.summary: What the corpus holds, and what it does not

get.description: Checks the API answers and PostgreSQL accepts a query.

The identifiers a work carries across platforms, and **how each link was established**: method, score, status.

No identifier is shared between Manga Sanctuary, Kitsu and Wikidata. Every link here is therefore a scored decision taken by a documented method, never a join on a common key. `method`, `score` and `status` are `null` when no decision has been recorded yet — 9 366 of 14 670 works have one. A work without a decision still exists: it answers 200, not 404.
Returns the cleaned Kitsu metadata for one series.

404.description: No Kitsu series with this identifier.

get.description: Checks the FastAPI process answers. Never touches PostgreSQL.
Returns the full text and metadata of a single RAG document.

404.description: No RAG document with this key.

get.description: Streams the entire RAG corpus, in full text, ordered by `doc_key`. Pagination is by opaque cursor and has no depth limit: follow `next_cursor` until it is `null` and every document has been seen exactly once. A page returning fewer than `limit` items is the last one; when the corpus size is an exact multiple of `limit`, a final empty page closes the walk.

get.description: Total document count and breakdown by source, with the timestamp of the measurement. Cursor pagination returns no total, so this is where a consumer learns how much there is to read before walking `/rag/export`.

That is what a preview is. To read the whole corpus, use `/rag/export`.

get.description:
Searches the series title, its other titles (`series_other_titles`) and its authors (writer, artist).

**Normalisation**: case-insensitive and accent-insensitive, through one character table applied to the columns and to the query alike.

**Ranking**: exact title, then title starting with the query, then title containing it (main title or another title), then author containing it; then `members_votes` descending, then `series_id`. `correspondance` says what answered, `titre_correspondant` which other title did.

**No typo tolerance**: a typo finds nothing — the application says so and points to the adviser. No result is `200` with `items: []`, never 404.

`offset` is capped at 1 000: a search returning more than 1 000 series is a query that is too short.

parameters.description: Title or author, 2 to 100 characters once stripped.
parameters.name: q

schema.description: Title or author, 2 to 100 characters once stripped.
schema.title: Q

get.description:
The catalogue record: titles, authors, publication data, ratings and review aggregates.

**Genres come in two fields, and neither replaces the other.** `genres_source` holds the raw French labels Manga Sanctuary wrote (12 652 series); `genres_enriched` holds normalised codes merged from both sources and expanded through the genre hierarchy (12 952 series). No `COALESCE` is applied here: collapsing them would invent a definition of *genre* that exists nowhere in the database. *The API exposes; it does not create.*

404.description: No series with this identifier. Distinct from an empty collection: a series with no volume or no review answers 200 with `items: []`.

get.summary: One series from the Manga Sanctuary catalogue

get.description:
Reads **`manga.ms_reviews_all`** — the complete review reference, 11 074 rows.

This is deliberately **not** `manga.ms_reviews` (3 187 rows), the legacy RAG corpus: that table is a filtered subset built for retrieval, and serving it here would silently hide two thirds of what was collected. Reading a table is not rebuilding a corpus — the RAG corpus keeps its own source and its own endpoints.

404.description: No series with this identifier. Distinct from an empty collection: a series with no volume or no review answers 200 with `items: []`.

get.description:
Tomaison, EAN, publisher, format and page count — what a bookseller actually sells. Ordered by volume number, `NULL` last.

`ean` is the barcode **as the source displayed it**, unvalidated: its checked reading lives in `manga.volume_identity`.

**Two fields carry a known source defect** and say so in their own description: `editeur` (a captured label, not a publisher) and `status` (a doubled label). They are served as collected rather than quietly dropped — a defect that is visible can be fixed.

Paginated with `limit`/`offset` rather than a cursor — see `/rag/export` for the opposite choice and its reason.
